findings.reason: the undecided route is the only path by which a family reaches the lead, so binding it to the superseded decision leaves a non-empty set of families with no lawful state under the section's own gate, and the node would discover this only at the read-back.
findings.text: §3 says "A family §2 reports undecided is not left split unseen", but the same paragraph says "this section applies §5's decision, not §2's alone". Widening the offered options from a member's source domains to every catalog domain spreads the probability mass over more candidates, so the set of families whose answer falls below the confidence floor under §5's options is not the set §2 reports. A family that clears the floor under §2's narrow options but not under §5's wide ones is neither carried to the lead nor written, and §3's zero-split read-back has no allowance for it: the read-back admits only "families held split by a recorded lead correction that names the family", and this family has no correction because nobody was asked.

findings.reason: it adds one free reading on an already-committed label set and closes the only regression path §5 can silently take.
findings.text: §5 changes the option set of the one family decision, and §2 done-when bullet 3 guards its regression on "the labelled names the domain decision was calibrated on in `sn-catalog-grouping`, almost all of them single-member families, the accuracy is recorded as a regression reading and is not lower". §5 replaces that option set for exactly those single-member families and re-reads only a fresh 60-name draw and §2's multi-member family label set. The calibration set (`scg-domain-label-sheet.json`, 73 rows, the pre-registered bar on which the incumbent reaches 58/73) is the population the widening is most likely to move, and nothing in §5 re-reads it, so a widening that gains on the new draw while losing on the calibration rows ships with every gate green.

findings.reason: the two populations must be reported separately (the planted names and the random draw) or the gate cannot distinguish a widened decision that is better from one that is merely different on the cases already known to be wrong.
findings.text: the 60 single-member names are "drawn across every domain file" with `safety_factor`, `greenwald_density` and `voltage_of_valve` "among them", and the gate is that the decision's share under the reader's domain "is higher" than the stored domains'. Those three are named in §1 and §5 precisely because their stored domain is known to be wrong, so their inclusion lowers the incumbent's share by up to 3/60 for free: a decision that agrees with the stored domain on all 57 randomly drawn names and differs only on the three planted ones passes, which is the plan restating §1's own examples rather than measuring the widening.

findings.reason: the followup is the section's dispatch brief, and the only place a coordinator reads what §3 waits on; a stale prerequisite there dispatches §3 against a missing decision.
findings.text: the followup body reads "§2 is ready. §3 writes the live graph and waits for §2; §4 waits for §3", while `_document`'s `plan-section-depends-on` now declares `"s3": ["sn-domain-per-family#s2", "sn-domain-per-family#s5"]`. §5 is a new unbuilt section, so the followup names `§2` as the whole of §3's prerequisite and omits the section §3 now waits on; a coordinator reading the followup dispatches §3 as soon as §2 lands, and §3's own text then applies a §5 decision that does not exist.

findings.reason: the sibling sections establish the directory and a worker will follow it, so this costs one clause and misdirects no mechanism; recorded so the author can name it in passing.
findings.text: §3's read-back, the before/after transport and general shares, the twenty largest moves and the spend are all "recorded" with no path named, while §2 and §5 each name `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-domain-per-family/`; §3 is the section whose evidence describes the live graph after a write, so it is the one whose record a later reader most needs to open.
